<reason>B wins the central comparative clash. A establishes plausible consolidation harms and eventually supplies a risk-based enforcement filter, but does not adequately establish its net benefits. B answers both pressure questions directly, distinguishes reduced rivalry from eliminated competition, and exposes A’s exclusion of productivity savings unless passed through to consumers—despite the motion explicitly counting productivity. A’s closing then mistakes uncertain pass-through for proof of no benefit rather than answering B’s strongest objections.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B decisively challenges A’s claim that mistaken clearance causes permanent harm while mistaken blocking merely delays commercialization. Financing constraints and missed development windows can prevent a product from emerging altogether. This directly undermines A’s principal weighing argument that alternative arrangements preserve innovation at only temporary cost.</best_rebuttal>
